answer.says: You are right. The system of needs has no patience for a man who has finished his consumption. I yield the particular space to the universal flow.
answer.thought: The bookseller’s impatience is the necessary limit of civil society: the particular individual must withdraw when his needs are satisfied, so that the system may continue its motion. I have no business remaining in the queue, and the air quality is already at 100, which is no place for a man who has finished his meal. I will return home to rest before the evening, as the sun is already setting.
